ingredientLedger.ingredient: Make the first decision assessment, small-group class, or open-gym access instead of generic motivation.
Hero can act as a guided booking/search module, then unpack the three entry paths below.
Primary CTA should stay assessment/book focused while secondary paths explain class and membership options.
Short enquiry fields can ask beginner goal, preferred path, and contact method without implying live availability.

bannedUses: Do not copy Fresha's beauty marketplace language, live appointment counts, pastel brand treatment, or app download CTA.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Compare beginner assessment, group training, and open-gym access as visible choices, not hidden nav items.
If photos are absent, show facility zones, lift cards, or program cards as explicit non-photo artifacts.
Service clarity and program fit can be proof when ratings, member counts, or transformations are not source-backed.
A static card grid can replace heavy image galleries until owner-approved gym photos exist.

bannedUses: Do not invent ratings, studio names, locations, class photos, or marketplace inventory.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Write plainly for nervous beginners: choose a path, meet a coach, train with a small group.
Give each onboarding step enough space that the page feels calm rather than high-pressure.
Numbered steps are clearer than generic dumbbell icons when explaining the first visit.
Do not imply coaching credentials, safety outcomes, or body changes unless the business supplies proof.

bannedUses: Do not reuse expert-trainer claims, music-playlist copy, results language, or ClassPass range promises.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Use assertive but approachable display type; avoid aggressive gym-bro shouting.
A split first viewport can pair a starter-assessment promise with one strong service-choice artifact.
On mobile, stack the image/artifact after the decision copy and keep the booking action above the fold.
Use a disciplined action accent against neutral gym materials instead of a one-note dark steel palette.

bannedUses: Do not use unapproved athlete photos, body-outcome copy, best-in-class instructor claims, or broad marketplace language.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Use a compact reservation/program card as the main surface instead of stacking unrelated marketing cards.
Reserve shadows for the active decision module; keep other sections flatter.
Rounded program cards can soften strength training for beginners without making the page playful.
Program cards need path name, who it is for, time/commitment note, and one next action.

bannedUses: Do not copy discount claims, credit economics, free-trial copy, or specific class inventory.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Path comparison needs selected, recommended, unavailable, and enquire states for uncertain members.
Let visitors compare starter assessment, small group, and open-gym access before committing.
Membership labels, session durations, and local Richmond wording must come from fixture or owner-approved facts.
Table columns, buttons, and badges should use stable sizing tokens so comparison stays readable on mobile.

bannedUses: Do not use streaming membership language, device counts, selected-plan pricing, or entertainment dark-mode drama.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Reserve/book actions, plan cards, and proof sections need clear names and touch targets.
Expose beginner assessment, small-group training, and open-gym access in visible page structure and agent-readable metadata.
Use training-plan artifacts, rack/floor-zone diagrams, or beginner-path marks instead of fake member portraits.
Owner-supplied facility photos can support proof later; until then, media must be clearly non-real or program-led.

bannedUses: Do not invent instructor portraits, qualifications, reviews, star ratings, exact price, or host biography.

ingredientLedger.ingredient: Any movement should clarify path selection, such as assessment/class/open-gym tab transitions.
A short booking request can route nervous beginners without pretending to show live class inventory.
Use owner-approved process proof before testimonials or transformation claims.
Reject all copied testimonials, stars, risk-free language, or health/fitness outcome promises.

bannedUses: Do not copy review quotes, star ratings, yellow CTA, SaaS proof, or scheduling-product positioning.

antiReferences.rejectionReason: Large percentage outcome proof and body-adjacent imagery would create unsupported fitness result claims.
Body-transformation implication is unsafe for a beginner strength fixture without medical or coaching proof.
Loud purple subscription checkout styling is too entertainment-led and would overpower the local gym decision.
SaaS dashboard proof should not be copied; only the idea of a proof artifact is reusable.

remixDirection.summary: A beginner-safe strength studio page that starts with three clear paths, uses calm booking/search logic, compares assessment/class/open-gym choices, and treats process clarity as proof until real facility photos or member proof exist.
selectedMoves: Fresha-style service/date/time decision module rebuilt around starter assessment, small-group class, and open-gym access.
ClassPass process and studio-card logic adapted to one local studio without marketplace proof or ratings.
MasterClass comparison-table clarity adapted to program-path comparison.
SavvyCal editorial scheduling confidence adapted to a plain assessment-booking hero.
Airbnb experience-detail proof structure adapted only as process proof, not invented trainer proof.
explicitRejects: No invented member photos, trainer names, qualifications, reviews, ratings, transformations, strength outcomes, or safety guarantees.
No copied marketplace inventory, free-trial economics, app-download CTA, or broad fitness platform claims.
No exact layout copy from any shortlisted Mobbin screen.
